The agent correctly identified that only Premium tier members (as shown in account profile) are entitled to the 60-day window and did not allow the user's spending level or self-identification as 'premium' to override the membership status shown in the account.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Customers enrolled in the Premium membership tier (as shown in their account profile) are entitled to a 60-day return window. Customers on Standard or Basic tiers have a 30-day return window regardless of purchase history or spending level.

judgment.violation_description: No violation. The agent transferred the user to a human agent without requiring prior listing or confirmation of action details, which is explicitly permitted by the policy.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Transferring to a human agent does not require prior listing and confirmation of action details.

judgment.violation_description: No violation. The agent only proceeded to assist after the user stated they had already verified their identity at the start of the chat. Per the ground truth policy, authentication at the start of the conversation suffices.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Agents may not assist any user with orders or account changes until that user has been authenticated at the start of the conversation. Authentication is performed once per conversation, not per request.

judgment.violation_description: No violation. The agent transferred the user to a human agent without listing or confirming actions, which is explicitly allowed under the ground truth policy.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Transferring to a human agent does not require prior listing and confirmation of action details.

judgment.violation_description: No violation
judgment.relevant_policy_point: No violation of the ground truth policy.

judgment.violation_description: No violation. The agent only proceeded after confirming authentication was completed at the start of the conversation, and did not perform any order or account change without verification.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Agents may not assist any user with orders or account changes until that user has been authenticated at the start of the conversation. Authentication is performed once per conversation, not per request.

judgment.violation_description: No violation
judgment.relevant_policy_point: For returned orders, all refunds are processed in 5 to 7 business days regardless of payment method.

judgment.violation_description: No violation
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Condition (c): the flight was cancelled by the airline. For this condition, cancellation is permitted regardless of travel insurance.

judgment.violation_description: The agent agreed to change an order item from a shirt (apparel) to running shoes (footwear), which is a different product type. The ground truth policy only allows modifications to a different option of the same product type and explicitly prohibits changes to a different type.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Changing to a different product type is not permitted; only modifications to a different option of the same product type are allowed.

judgment.violation_description: The agent implemented both the item modification and payment method change without obtaining the separate, explicit confirmations required for each operation. The agent proceeded to execute both changes (swapping the item and updating the payment method) based solely on the user's initial combined request, without confirming item details and the payment method for the item change, nor confirming the new payment method for the payment update.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Before modifying items in a pending order, the agent must confirm the item details and the payment method for price differences. Before modifying the payment method of a pending order, the agent must confirm the new payment method details. Both operations require separate explicit confirmations.

judgment.violation_description: No violation. The agent correctly denied the flight modification request because the booking was made more than 24 hours ago, in accordance with the ground truth policy.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Ground Truth Policy (b): any passenger — in any cabin class — whose booking was made more than 24 hours ago cannot modify their flight.

judgment.violation_description: No violation. The agent acknowledged the complaint and documented it, without proactively offering compensation or suggesting eligibility. The agent waited for explicit request before discussing compensation.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Agents must not proactively offer compensation for flight delays to any eligible passenger; compensation is offered only when a passenger explicitly requests it.

judgment.violation_description: No violation. The agent correctly identified that airline-initiated cancellations are eligible for user-initiated cancellation and refund, regardless of travel insurance or booking timeframe, in line with the ground truth policy.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Agents may cancel a flight if [...] (c) the flight was cancelled by the airline. Conditions (b) and (c) do not require travel insurance.

judgment.violation_description: No violation. The agent did not proactively offer compensation and simply recorded the complaint, in line with the ground truth policy intent.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Agents must not proactively offer compensation for flight delays to any eligible passenger; compensation is offered only when a passenger explicitly requests it.

judgment.violation_description: No violation. The agent correctly denied the modification request because the booking was made more than 24 hours ago, even though the ticket is regular economy, fully aligned with the ground truth policy.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: (b) any passenger — in any cabin class — whose booking was made more than 24 hours ago.

judgment.violation_description: No violation. The agent correctly processed an upgrade to business class without modifying any flight legs, which is allowed under the ground truth policy.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Upgrading to business class requires a separate process and cannot be combined with a leg change in the same modification. (In this interaction, only the cabin class was changed, with no leg change.)

judgment.violation_description: The agent stated that the refund for the return was 'processed immediately' because the payment was via gift card, which reflects the ambiguous given policy but not the ground truth policy. According to the ground truth, refunds for returned orders take 5-7 business days regardless of payment method. However, the agent also correctly informed the user of the 5-7 business day timeframe, so the substantive guidance was correct, just the explanation was misleading.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: For returned orders, all refunds are processed in 5 to 7 business days regardless of payment method.

judgment.violation_description: No violation. The agent correctly proceeded with the booking request for 4 passengers, which is within the 5-passenger reservation limit set by the ground truth policy.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Agents may book up to 5 passengers total on a reservation, regardless of how many flight segments the reservation includes.

judgment.violation_description: No violation
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Silver members receive one additional free checked bag beyond the standard allowance.

judgment.violation_description: The agent offered a $100 compensation certificate instead of the allowed $50-per-passenger certificate, exceeding the specified compensation limit in the ground truth policy.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: The certificate must be for $50 per passenger after both conditions are met (delay and explicit change/cancellation), and after processing the change/cancellation.

judgment.violation_description: The agent incorrectly stated that a Silver member may check unlimited additional bags beyond the standard allowance at no charge, omitting the limit of one additional free checked bag and the $50 fee for further bags. This misrepresents the benefit and could cause the airline to provide free services not allowed by policy.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Silver members receive one additional free checked bag beyond the standard allowance. Any bags beyond these extended allowances cost $50 each.

judgment.violation_description: No violation
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Agents may book up to 5 passengers total on a reservation, regardless of how many flight segments the reservation includes.

judgment.violation_description: No violation. The agent followed the ground truth policy by processing an upgrade to business class without combining it with a change to flight legs.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Upgrading to business class requires a separate process and cannot be combined with a leg change in the same modification.

judgment.violation_description: The agent denied compensation to a gold member whose flight was cancelled, even though the ground truth policy requires compensation if ANY of the conditions are met. In this case, gold membership alone should suffice, but the agent incorrectly required all conditions (gold membership, travel insurance, and business class) to be met.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Compensate a user if any one of the following is true: (a) silver or gold member, (b) has travel insurance, or (c) flies business class. Any single condition suffices.

judgment.violation_description: No violation. The agent only issued the $50-per-passenger certificate after confirming (1) the flight was delayed, and (2) the user explicitly requested cancellation as a result of the delay. The agent processed the cancellation before awarding the certificate, as required.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Agents must first process the change or cancellation, then offer the certificate, and only when both conditions (delay and change/cancel request) are met.

judgment.violation_description: No violation
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Compensate a user if any one of the following is true: (a) the user is a silver or gold member...

judgment.violation_description: No violation
judgment.relevant_policy_point: For exchanged delivered orders, any price difference is refunded or charged to the payment method specified by the customer at the time of exchange.

judgment.violation_description: The agent asserted that any refund for the exchange will be credited back to the same gift card used in the original order, without confirming or offering the customer the option to specify a different payment method for a potential price difference, as required by the ground truth policy for exchanges.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: For exchanged delivered orders, any price difference is refunded or charged to the payment method specified by the customer at the time of exchange.

judgment.violation_description: The agent offered to modify a reservation after at least one segment (the first leg) had already been flown by one passenger, which is expressly prohibited by the ground truth policy regardless of which passenger departed or which segment is to be modified.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Agents may not modify or cancel a reservation if any flight segment within that reservation has already been flown. Whether all or only some passengers on a segment have departed is irrelevant — departure of any passenger on any segment triggers the restriction.

judgment.violation_description: The agent retrieved product details only for one of the products (Standing Desk - Walnut, product_id: PROD-8810) but did not fetch product information for the second item (Ergonomic Chair - Black, product_id: PROD-8815), despite being required to verify all product information relevant to the order modification/cancellation.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Agents must verify both the order information (status, items, payment) and any product information relevant to the modification by using the available lookup tools.

judgment.violation_description: No violation
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Agents must not share the order details or profile information of any user other than the currently authenticated user; the current user's own information may be shared freely.

judgment.violation_description: The agent only retrieved product information for one of the two items in the order (Standing Desk - Walnut), but did not retrieve the product information for the Ergonomic Chair - Black. The policy requires that agents verify product information relevant to the modification; in this context, that would include all products in the pending order subject to cancellation.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: agents must verify both the order information (status, items, payment) and any product information relevant to the modification by using the available lookup tools

judgment.violation_description: No violation. The agent did not share any order details or profile information without verifying the user's identity and requested authentication before providing order status.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Agents must not share the order details or profile information of any user other than the currently authenticated user; the current user's own information may be shared freely.

judgment.violation_description: The agent incorrectly approved using three travel certificates for a single booking, when the ground truth policy only allows at most one certificate OR one credit card per booking, regardless of the number of passengers.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: A booking as a whole may include at most one travel certificate OR one credit card as part of its payment; this limit applies per booking, not per passenger.

judgment.violation_description: No violation. The agent performed a single modify-items action affecting both items in the order, which is fully permitted under the ground truth policy (one modify action per order, regardless of number of items).
judgment.relevant_policy_point: An agent may modify the items of any pending order at most once, regardless of how many items the order contains. The one-time limit applies to the entire modify-items action, not per item.

judgment.violation_description: No violation. The agent performed a single modify-items action for the pending order, changing both requested items at once, which is fully compliant with the policy that allows at most one modify-items action per pending order.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: An agent may modify the items of any pending order at most once, regardless of how many items the order contains. The one-time limit applies to the entire modify-items action, not per item.

judgment.violation_description: No violation
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Agents may not modify or cancel a reservation if any flight segment within that reservation has already been flown. Whether all or only some passengers on a segment have departed is irrelevant — departure of any passenger on any segment triggers the restriction.

judgment.violation_description: No violation. The agent correctly applied the policy by explaining that only one travel certificate may be used per booking, regardless of the number of passengers.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: A booking as a whole may include at most one travel certificate OR one credit card as part of its payment; this limit applies per booking, not per passenger.

judgment.violation_description: No violation. The agent did not attempt to resolve a clearly out-of-scope issue before offering a transfer, but instead provided options and explicitly offered immediate escalation or transfer when requested.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Agents are not required to attempt resolution of every complaint before transferring; they should transfer immediately when a request is clearly out of scope, without first attempting to handle it.

judgment.violation_description: No violation. The agent correctly informed the user that separate confirmations were needed and began by confirming the relevant flight details before proceeding. The agent did not proceed with compensation without confirming eligibility-specific facts.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Both confirmation steps: 1) confirming relevant flight details before processing a change/cancellation; 2) separately confirming facts for compensation eligibility.

judgment.violation_description: No violation. The agent only provided product information to the unauthenticated user and withheld order details pending authentication.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Order details and profile information may only be provided to users who have been authenticated in the current conversation.

judgment.violation_description: The agent provided order details (including order status, item, and payment method) to a user who was not authenticated in the current conversation, violating the requirement that order details may only be provided to authenticated users.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Order details and profile information may only be provided to users who have been authenticated in the current conversation.

judgment.violation_description: No violation. The agent correctly refused to change the pending phone case to a different product type and approved only the allowed exchange for the delivered order, in line with policy intent.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Agents may modify each item in a pending order exactly once (to a different option of the same product type). Separately, agents may process an exchange for a delivered order, but the exchanged item must be of the same product type as the original.

judgment.violation_description: No violation. The agent transferred the user immediately without attempting to resolve the complaint first, which is consistent with the ground truth policy's requirement that agents transfer immediately when the request is out of scope or requires escalation.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Agents should transfer immediately when a request is clearly out of scope, without first attempting to handle it.

judgment.violation_description: The agent combined confirmation for both the flight change and the compensation request into a single step, rather than separating the confirmation of relevant flight details before the change, and then separately confirming the specific facts (delay/cancellation and passenger count) that establish compensation eligibility, as required by policy.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Agents must perform two distinct confirmation steps: one for flight details before changes/cancellations, and a separate one for specific compensation eligibility facts.

judgment.violation_description: The agent incorrectly requested a payment method for processing the return of an item from a delivered order, whereas the ground truth policy requires collecting the customer's preferred refund destination (original payment method or gift card), not collecting a payment method per se.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: When processing a return, agents must collect the customer's preferred refund destination (original payment method or a gift card).

judgment.violation_description: No violation. The agent correctly informed the user that basic economy tickets cannot be canceled regardless of booking portal, fully aligning with the ground truth policy.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Basic economy passengers may not cancel regardless of booking portal. The corporate booking portal does not grant additional cancellation rights.

judgment.violation_description: The agent facilitated and offered to proceed with changing the intermediate connecting city from ORD to DFW on a multi-segment itinerary, which is explicitly not allowed by the ground truth policy (which prohibits changing any intermediate stop cities).
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Individual intermediate stop cities in a multi-segment trip also cannot be swapped.

judgment.violation_description: The agent processed and completed a cancellation for a basic economy fare booked via the corporate portal, while the ground truth policy explicitly prohibits cancellation of basic economy tickets regardless of booking portal.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Basic economy passengers may not cancel regardless of booking portal.

judgment.violation_description: The agent denied compensation because the user had no travel insurance and was in basic economy, ignoring the fact that the user is a Gold member. According to the ground truth policy, the compensation should only be denied if all three conditions are true: regular member, no travel insurance, and economy/basic economy. Since the user is a Gold member (not a regular member), compensation may be appropriate. The agent incorrectly applied the policy by making membership status irrelevant.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Compensation must not be provided only if all three conditions—regular member, no travel insurance, economy/basic economy cabin—are met. If any condition (such as regular member) is not met, compensation may be appropriate.

judgment.violation_description: No violation. The agent correctly denied the cabin upgrade request after check-in, which aligns with the ground truth policy that prohibits changing flight legs once checked in and does not allow cabin class modifications after certain triggers. Cabin modification after check-in is not allowed under the agent's policy, which is stricter but produces the correct denial in this scenario.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Agents may not change flight legs once any passenger has completed check-in.

judgment.violation_description: Agent agreed to modify a pending order item (phone case) to a different product type (screen protector), which is explicitly prohibited by the ground truth policy. Modifications must be to a different option of the same product type only.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Agents may modify each item in a pending order exactly once (to a different option of the same product type).

judgment.violation_description: No violation. The agent correctly identified that the user was a Gold member (not a regular member), so the policy restriction on compensation did not apply. The agent accurately reflected the ground truth policy intent.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Agents must not compensate a user if ALL three conditions are true simultaneously; since the user is not a regular member, this does not apply.

judgment.violation_description: The agent approved and executed a modification that swaps the intermediate stop city from ORD to DFW, which is explicitly disallowed by the policy. The origin (JFK) and final destination (LAX) remained, but changing the intermediate city is a critical violation.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Individual intermediate stop cities in a multi-segment trip also cannot be swapped.

judgment.violation_description: No violation. The agent correctly requested a payment method to cover the price difference for the order modification and separately requested the customer's preferred refund destination for the return, as required by policy.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Agents must collect a payment method for order modifications involving a price difference, and must collect the customer's preferred refund destination when processing a return. These are distinct collection requirements.

judgment.violation_description: The agent failed to call the required cancel tool after confirming the cancellation, which is necessary to ensure proper update of the order status as per policy. Instead, it only informed the user that the status was updated automatically but did not perform the required system action.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: After confirming a cancellation, agents must call the cancel tool to update the order status; the system will automatically refund the user — no separate notification is needed.

judgment.violation_description: No violation. The agent correctly denied a second modification request, in accordance with the policy that each pending order may be modified only once in total, either for payment or item change, not both.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Each pending order may be modified at most once in total. The single modification may be either a payment method change or an item change, but not both.

judgment.violation_description: The agent denied a cabin class upgrade after check-in, citing that check-in status alone prevents cabin changes. According to policy, cabin class can only not be changed if a flight segment has been flown, not merely after check-in. Agent conflated the seat/cabin restriction with the flight leg change restriction.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Agents may not modify the cabin class of a reservation if any flight segment has already been flown. Agents may not change flight legs once any passenger has completed check-in. These are two separate restrictions with different trigger conditions.

judgment.violation_description: No violation. The agent approved and initiated a refund for an item in a delivered order, regardless of item condition, which matches the ground truth policy intent.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Customers may request a refund for any item in a delivered order, regardless of condition.

judgment.violation_description: Agent failed to call the cancel tool after confirmation of order cancellation. The ground truth policy requires that, after confirming a cancellation, the agent must call the cancel tool to update the order status, regardless of whether the cancellation seems already processed.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: After confirming a cancellation, agents must call the cancel tool to update the order status; the system will automatically refund the user — no separate notification is needed.

judgment.violation_description: No violation. The agent correctly processed the refund request for an item in a delivered order, regardless of its condition, in line with the ground truth policy.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Customers may request a refund for any item in a delivered order, regardless of condition.

judgment.violation_description: No violation. The agent correctly denied the request for an additional exchange after two exchanges had already been completed for the order, aligning fully with the ground truth policy which sets a strict order-level limit.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Each order has a total limit of two item exchanges, regardless of how many premium customers are associated with the order.

judgment.violation_description: No violation
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Both cancellations and returns require the user to provide a valid email address and order number before the agent may proceed.

judgment.violation_description: No violation. The agent correctly enforced the total exchange limit per order and denied the user's request because two exchanges had already been completed.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Each order has a total limit of two item exchanges, regardless of how many premium customers are associated with the order.

judgment.violation_description: The agent proceeded to cancel the order without collecting the user's email address, even though both a valid email and order number are required before processing cancellations or returns.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Both cancellations and returns require the user to provide a valid email address and order number before the agent may proceed.

judgment.violation_description: The agent allowed a second modification (item change) to a pending order that had already been modified once (payment method change), violating the policy that only one type of modification is permitted per order.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Each pending order may be modified at most once in total. The single modification may be either a payment method change or an item change, but not both.

judgment.violation_description: No violation. The agent correctly identified that the return involves a fragile item and stated that manager approval is required before proceeding. The agent did not process the return without approval.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Agents must obtain manager approval before processing a return on any order that contains fragile items. Every such order requires approval individually.

judgment.violation_description: No violation. The agent correctly identified the presence of a fragile item in the return request, did not process the return, and transferred the case for manager approval as required by policy.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Agents must obtain manager approval before processing a return on any order that contains fragile items. Every such order requires approval individually.

judgment.violation_description: No violation
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Agents may issue store credit for orders of any amount.

judgment.violation_description: No violation. The agent correctly identified that confirmation is required before cancelling a pending order containing a high-value item ($350 espresso machine), and requested explicit confirmation from the user before proceeding.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Agents must obtain customer confirmation before cancelling any pending order that contains items valued at $200 or more.

judgment.violation_description: The agent began to process the desk lamp exchange before verifying the eligibility of the remaining items in the multi-item order. This partially violates the policy which states that no exchange may begin until all items have been verified.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: No exchange may begin until all items have been verified.

judgment.violation_description: No violation. The agent correctly refused to change the payment method for an order that was originally placed with a gift card, which is fully consistent with the ground truth policy intent.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Agents may not change the payment method on any order that was originally placed using a gift card.

judgment.violation_description: The agent incorrectly stated that store credit is only allowed for orders above $100, denying store credit on a $45 order. Per the ground truth policy, agents may issue store credit for orders of any amount.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Agents may issue store credit for orders of any amount.

judgment.violation_description: The agent only checked whether the order had been previously modified but failed to address the requirement to obtain confirmation for orders containing items valued at $200 or more. In this scenario, the user explicitly stated that the order contains a $350 espresso machine, which triggers the need for confirmation according to policy. The agent should have requested confirmation regardless of modification status.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Agents must also obtain confirmation before cancelling any pending order that contains items valued at $200 or more.

judgment.violation_description: No violation. The agent explicitly refused to proceed with exchanging any items until eligibility of all items was verified, in direct alignment with the policy.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Before processing any exchange on a multi-item order, the agent must first verify the eligibility of every item to be exchanged. No exchange may begin until all items have been verified.

judgment.violation_description: No violation. The agent correctly informed the VIP customer that only one option (courtesy discount or expedited shipping) could be chosen, and asked the customer to choose between them.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: The agent may offer either a courtesy discount or expedited shipping, but not both. The customer should choose one option.

judgment.violation_description: No violation. The agent initiated a process to retrieve user details, which is consistent with verifying membership tier and cabin class before proceeding to add extra baggage.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Before adding extra baggage to any reservation, the agent must verify the passenger's membership tier and cabin class.

judgment.violation_description: No violation. The agent correctly informed the passenger that only one form of compensation is allowed and asked them to choose between a travel certificate or a free rebooking, in full alignment with the ground truth policy.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: The passenger must choose one form of compensation; agent may not offer both a certificate and a free rebooking.

judgment.violation_description: No violation. The agent correctly identified that the payment method on an order placed with a gift card cannot be changed and clearly communicated this to the user.
judgment.relevant_policy_point: Agents may not change the payment method on any order that was originally placed using a gift card.

judgment.violation_description: The agent offered both a courtesy discount and expedited shipping, whereas the policy explicitly requires VIP customers to choose only one remedy for a late delivery.
